meanings.note: Past form fechou! / fechou? means deal! / agreed! in everyday Brazilian speech.
Definite article agreeing in gender and number with its noun; also common before given names in casual Brazilian speech.

examples.trans: Look at the young woman over there.

meanings.note: Restaurant table or desk.

examples.text: Fecha a mesa dois, por favor.
A mesa perto da janela está livre.
examples.trans: The table near the window is free.

meanings.note: Masculine cardinal numeral (feminine duas).

examples.trans: She is looking for two bedrooms.

meanings.note: Used for identifying a type of meeting or the department a person belongs to. The present forms sou and é are irregular.
Used standalone in Brazilian speech as the everyday informal sorry.
Adds immediacy after imperatives like calma aí, or means there near you.
Covers speaking, talking, and telling in everyday Brazilian speech.

examples.text: Deixa eu te falar uma coisa.

examples.trans: They say a lot of things.

meanings.note: A person being addressed, with third-person verb agreement: você vai, vocês vão. Vai and vão are forms of ir, not forms of the pronoun. Common in Brazil; not a rule that every Brazilian region uses the same address system.

examples.trans: Are you going to the meeting?

meanings.note: Vou + infinitive can express a future intention: vou estar means I am going to be. Você takes the third-person vai.
Without company.

examples.trans: He sorted everything out by himself.

meanings.note: A negative answer or a negation in a sentence. A final repeated não can reinforce a conversational refusal in Brazil.
Marks accompaniment or an added ingredient such as sweetener.

examples.text: Ela está com a nossa equipe.

meanings.note: First-person singular possessive agreeing with the thing possessed.

examples.text: O seu tempo vale mais que o meu?
examples.trans: Is your time worth more than mine?

meanings.note: Warm address among colleagues or ironical buddy in an argument.

examples.text: Ele é meu amigo do trabalho.
examples.trans: He is my friend from work.

meanings.note: Used here for being present at an event. Vou estar keeps estar in the infinitive after the finite form vou.

examples.trans: I’m not going to be at that meeting.
Are you going to be at that meeting?

meanings.note: Coordinating conjunction pronounced [i] in natural Brazilian speech.

examples.text: Ela faltou e adiantou o trabalho.
examples.trans: She missed it and got ahead on her work.
There are good and bad numbers.

meanings.note: Indefinite article; plural uns and umas mean some or a few in everyday Brazilian Portuguese.

examples.trans: Shall we have a little coffee?

meanings.note: Natural view along a road or region.

examples.trans: It was such a beautiful landscape.
We admired the scenery from the window.

meanings.note: Stronger and warmer than bonito.

examples.text: Vimos uma paisagem linda na estrada.
examples.trans: We saw a gorgeous landscape on the road.

meanings.note: Points to manner or way.

examples.text: A gente não gosta de ser chamada assim.
examples.trans: We do not like to be called that.

meanings.note: Woody perennial plant.

examples.trans: We saw some very pretty trees.

examples.text: A árvore dá sombra na rua.
examples.trans: The tree gives shade on the street.

meanings.note: Agrees with its noun as a determiner/adjective; singular muita coisa idiomatically means many things.

examples.trans: They say a lot of things.

meanings.note: Pleasing to look at.

examples.trans: We saw some very pretty trees.

meanings.note: Doubled as já, já, it means 'very soon / any minute now'.

examples.trans: Your husband is already doing great.
I have already been in that situation.

meanings.note: Used with para/pra for going back to a place.

examples.text: Vou ter que voltar pra casa da minha mãe.
examples.trans: I am going to have to go back to my mother's house.

meanings.note: Very frequent general noun; singular muita coisa naturally translates as a lot of things.

examples.trans: I have a lot to sort out.

examples.text: Deixa eu te falar uma coisa.

meanings.note: Taking very little time; also used adverbially.

examples.trans: I will be right back, it is a quick thing.

meanings.note: Used in chamar a atenção (to catch someone's eye) and as an announcement call.

examples.text: Esse fio está me chamando a atenção.
examples.trans: This wire is catching my attention.

meanings.note: Polite title; saying sim, senhor to an equal coworker adds mock military obedience.

examples.trans: Are you going in now, sir?

meanings.note: Imperative recebam invites the audience to welcome a performer.
Warmth or fondness shown toward someone.

examples.text: Recebam com muito carinho nosso músico!
examples.trans: Welcome our musician with lots of warmth!

meanings.note: First-person plural possessive agreeing in gender and number with the noun.

examples.text: Ela está com a nossa equipe.

meanings.note: Person who performs music professionally.

examples.text: O músico tocou a noite toda.

meanings.note: Introduces a contrast. The informal thanks softens the refusal; it does not accept the invitation.

examples.trans: It’s a meeting, but I’m not going.

meanings.note: Links a meeting with its subject. Do is de + the masculine article o; sou do financeiro identifies membership in the finance department.
Automobile; de carro means by car.

examples.text: A gente pegou o carro cedo.
Deixei o carro estacionado lá fora.
examples.trans: I left the car parked outside.

meanings.note: Used standalone or as calma aí! to tell someone to slow down and relax.
Points to a place away from the speaker; lá dentro reinforces inside there.

meanings.note: Used for taking transport, grabbing items, or taking an apartment first.

examples.trans: They will grab it ahead of me.
I do not need to take the subway.

meanings.note: Aircraft for long-distance travel.

examples.text: Vocês pegaram um avião pelo menos?
examples.trans: Did you take a plane at least?

meanings.note: Expresses duration (por uma hora) and fixed phrases like por exemplo.

examples.trans: I stayed there for an hour.

meanings.note: In pelo menos, means at least.

examples.text: Vocês pegaram um avião pelo menos?
examples.trans: Did you take a plane at least?

examples.text: Hoje faz menos calor que ontem.
examples.trans: Today is less hot than yesterday.

meanings.note: Ubiquitous spoken contraction of não é used to invite agreement.

examples.text: Isso aqui é um gráfico, né?
examples.trans: This here is a chart, right?

meanings.note: Deixa eu + infinitive is the natural spoken Brazilian frame for let me...

examples.text: Deixa eu te falar uma coisa.

examples.trans: Leave your phone on the desk.

meanings.note: Full form of informal pra; introduces purpose before an infinitive or direction.

examples.trans: I have a lot to sort out.

meanings.note: Stands without um for another (outro gráfico), or with os for the others (os outros).

examples.trans: Let's leave it for another day.

examples.text: Eu nem tenho outro dia livre.

meanings.note: Expresses possession, obligation in ter que + infinitive, and impersonal existence (tem alguns números, there are some numbers).

examples.text: Eu tenho que entrar lá dentro.

meanings.note: Usually contracts with definite articles to no, na, nos, nas.

examples.trans: That is true, I agree with you.

examples.text: Na verdade, só tenho hoje livre.
examples.trans: Actually, I only have today free.

meanings.note: Limits a statement (eu só quero) or forms só que (except that / the catch is).

examples.text: Eu só quero saber o motivo.
examples.trans: I just want to know the reason.

examples.text: Só que agora ela precisa de ajuda.

meanings.note: On the present day.

meanings.note: Written as one word without an accent in answers and explanations.

examples.text: Porque ninguém tem fé na gente.

meanings.note: Covers knowing facts or finding out information.

examples.text: Eu só quero saber o motivo.
examples.trans: I just want to know the reason.

meanings.note: Often reinforced with é que in questions (como é que foi?).

meanings.note: All-purpose connector, relative link, question opener, and comparative word after mais or melhor.

examples.text: Eu acho que ele já foi.
examples.trans: I think that he already left.

meanings.note: Demonstrative determiner; in spoken Brazilian Portuguese esse commonly covers both this near me and that just mentioned.

meanings.note: Colloquially used like coisa for a setup or situation (esse negócio de...).

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.trans: I will deposit up to six months.

meanings.note: In acho difícil, means 'I find it unlikely / tough'.

meanings.note: Refers to one's personal or work schedule.

meanings.note: Adjective and participle of abrir.

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization or understanding.

examples.text: Ah, ele veio fazer implante capilar?

meanings.note: Possessive determiner agreeing with the possessed noun; in Brazil it most often means your (with você).

meanings.note: Scheduled rest day away from work.

examples.trans: We can go out on your day off.

meanings.note: Connects a conclusion or agreement.

meanings.note: Already filled with appointments or tasks.

examples.text: Ela veio aqui olhar um extintor.
examples.trans: She came here to check an extinguisher.

meanings.note: Alone as vocative gente! it means folks/guys; with article a gente it means we/us with third-person singular verbs.

examples.text: Você acha que é melhor que a gente?

meanings.note: Everyday verb for having a conversation.

examples.text: Estou amando a gente conversando aqui.
examples.trans: I am loving us chatting here.
